correctness.rationale: Independent adjacency-constrained enumeration finds all 96 permutations and the stated 1,090 independent sets and 24,875 flag orbits. Face-size sequences distinguish the faces of a flag simplex, so it injects into the geometric quotient and its oriented facets are the signed deletions. The independent reconstruction replayed all 12,114 frozen collapse pairs and checked that the 647 surviving labels and signed boundaries match the frozen residual data exactly. On that residual it got ranks (13,70,144,96), solely a factor 2 in boundary degree four, and a trivial fundamental group by signed triangular relator elimination after a spanning tree. A different collapse order reached a different residual but the same integral homology and pi1. Since H2 vanishes, simple connectivity implies 2-connectivity by Hurewicz. The generator of pi3=H3=Z/2 is annihilated by degree two, so its representing sphere map extends over the fourth cell of M(Z/2,3). The extension is an integral homology equivalence between simply connected CW complexes and hence a homotopy equivalence.
residual_risks: Exact finite reproduction and CW arguments apply only to this graph and the full action. No formal verification or claim about other subgroup quotients.

value.rationale: For a standard highly symmetric graph, the same full quotient was known to be rationally acyclic. The complete integral homotopy description now distinguishes it from a point, locates its unique torsion precisely and establishes 2-connectivity; these are meaningful facts about this symmetry action that rational representations cannot deliver.
residual_risks: This is a single natural orbit space, not a general result on generalized Petersen graphs.
